original.target_description: Aguado et al. (2009), Experiment 1A; participant-based face expression × face sex interaction in sex-classification error proportions, not the expression-classification task or a comparison between tasks.

n.sample_role: Participants assigned to the sex-classification condition (half of the 32 participants); analytic test F(1,15).
n.exclusions: No participant exclusion reported for this test.
n.location: p. 11, Experiment 1A Participants; p. 12, Classification Task: Error Rates
n.quote: Participants were 32 first- and second-year psychology students ... Half of the participants were randomly assigned to the expression condition, and the other half to the sex condition.

es.quote: a significant interaction between face expression and face sex was obtained [F(1,15) = 27.11, p < .001, ηp² = .64].

replication.target_description: Lipp et al. (2015), Experiment 1a; repeated-measures Sex × Expression interaction in sex-categorization error percentages, 32-individual stimulus set.

n.sample_role: Participants in Experiment 1a, all completing sex and expression categorization; error-test F(1,23).
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions reported for Experiment 1a. Reaction-time trimming (faster than 100 ms or outside three individual SDs) is described separately; no error-data participant exclusion stated.
n.location: p. 1287 (PDF p. 3), Participants, Procedure, and Results
n.quote: A total of 24 volunteers (four males, 20 females) received course credit in return for their participation.

es.location: p. 1287 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1a Results, sex categorization errors
es.quote: a Sex × Expression interaction, F(1, 23) = 62.13, p < .001, ηp² = .730.

p.location: p. 1287 (PDF p. 3), Experiment 1a Results, sex categorization errors

reported_success.quote: The results of Experiment 1a provided a direct replication of Aguado et al. (2009) in a within-subjects design and using the same faces that had been used in the original study.

notes: Both primary-paper titles and DOIs verified from full PDF text. Original n=16 is explicitly established by equal assignment of 32 participants to two conditions, corroborated by F(1,15); not the full-paper total of 32. Replication authors report an Experiment 1a-level direct-replication verdict; it is not a separately worded error-only verdict. PDF extraction loses some original mathematical glyphs; equations are transcribed with normalized mathematical notation.
